collection_summary: This instance is a source-defined ground truth listing the 26 Booker Prize for Fiction winners 2000-2024 inclusive (25 award years + 1 extra row for the 2019 co-winner Bernardine Evaristo + Margaret Atwood shared prize), with the winning book and the author's birth country derived from the per-author Wikipedia article's 'Born' field. The composite primary key (Year, Author) cleanly handles the 2019 co-winners and the 2 within-window 2-time winners (Hilary Mantel 2009 + 2012; Margaret Atwood 2000 + 2019). The schema is designed for implicit_join benchmark evaluation: Year + Author + Book are directly from the master Booker Prize winners table; Author Birth Country is the implicit-join cell requiring per-author Wikipedia article lookup. claim_type = source_defined because the row universe is the Booker winners table filtered to Year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2024 — the 25-year time window is curator-chosen but membership inside that window is fully source-defined.
source_coverage_notes:
Roles:
- source_urls[0] (Booker_Prize): master article supplying universe + filter + 3 of 4 cells per row. The Booker Prize Wikipedia article's winners table contains Year + Author + Book columns for all 25 award years 2000-2024 inclusive (with 2 rows for 2019 co-winners). The staged universe is fully defined by this master article's table membership filtered to the 2000-2024 inclusive window.
- source_urls[1-24] (24 per-author Wikipedia articles): per-author source supplying Author Birth Country (the implicit-join cell). Each author's article 'Born' field in the infobox names the modern sovereign country of the author's birthplace; for authors born in constituent countries (Anna Burns born in Belfast / Northern Ireland; Douglas Stuart born in Glasgow / Scotland), the constituent-country normalization rule applies (Northern Ireland / Scotland → United Kingdom).

Multi-source Tier B instance (source_count = 25 = 1 master + 24 per-author articles). The 24 per-author articles cover 24 distinct authors; Hilary Mantel and Margaret Atwood each won twice within the window but have only one Wikipedia article each. Cell-level audit: Year / Author / Book cells can be spot-checked against the master Booker Prize winners table; Author Birth Country can be spot-checked against the per-author article's 'Born' field with the constituent-country normalization applied.

Implicit-join structure: master Booker article gives (Year, Author, Book) as a denormalized winners table; per-author Wikipedia articles supply the Author Birth Country cell — a clean single-master-multiple-per-entity implicit join matching the precedent set by nato_accessions_1999_2024_capitals (master gives Country+Year; per-country article gives Capital) and notable_works_of_recent_nobel_literature_laureates (master gives Laureate; Wikidata SPARQL supplies Works).
decision_log:
Candidate card (per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: Pass (after pre-staging audit design review — see post-staging cycle-0 notes below). Universe (26 Booker Prize for Fiction winners 2000-2024 inclusive) is fully source-defined via the master Booker Prize Wikipedia article's winners table filtered to the 25-year window. Per-row attribute cells are verbatim from the master (Year + Author + Book) or grounded by per-author Wikipedia articles (Author Birth Country). Table is LLM-knowable for a pre-2025 cutoff: very-LLM-knowable cells include canonical Booker winners (Atwood 2000, Mantel 2009/2012, Barnes 2011); mid-difficulty cells include the well-known but less-headline-grabbing winners (Adiga 2008, Flanagan 2014, James 2015); harder calibration cells include the recent/less-known winners (Lynch 2023, Karunatilaka 2022, Harvey 2024). Row count (26) clears the 10-row gate.
- Seed/provenance: original instance, NOT from a seed in example_questions.txt. User selected after picker recommendation for 'chip implicit_join from gap-3 to gap-2' option; pre-staging audit design review (1 round) resolved 4 design-level cleanups before any files were written.
- Category: implicit_join (gap 3 before this staging — `implicit_join` at 5 of 8 with nato_accessions_1999_2024_capitals, notable_works_of_recent_nobel_literature_laureates, landmark_us_supreme_court_decisions_by_chief_justice, and 2 registered trial_join_*; this instance brings implicit_join to 6 of 8 — gap 3 → 2).
- Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, multi-source; gt_construction = manual_wikipedia; source_count = 25 (1 master + 24 per-author articles).
- Expected shape: 26 rows × 4 columns; composite PK = (Year, Author).
- Domain: Culture/Literature — extends the Culture/Literature subdomain from 1 instance (notable_works_of_recent_nobel_literature_laureates) to 2.
- Entity class: people/authors — NEW fine-class within the people bucket (people bucket currently has 9 fine-classes: politicians, scientists, athletes, painters, philosophers, laureates, deities, honorees, astronauts; this instance adds authors as the 10th).
- Risks/adaptation: (a) 25-year window 2000-2024 is curator-chosen but membership inside is source-defined; audit confirmed this is acceptable claim_type = source_defined; the universe rule documents the explicit window. (b) The 2019 co-winners (Bernardine Evaristo + Margaret Atwood) are handled by the composite PK as 2 rows with Year=2019. (c) 2-time winners (Hilary Mantel 2009 + 2012; Margaret Atwood 2000 + 2019) are handled by the composite PK as multiple rows with same Author + different Year + different Book. (d) Author Birth Country cell uses bare country names without parenthetical disambiguations per the audit-recommended modern-sovereign-country normalization rule; citizenship/nationality/raised-in facts are documented in normalization_decisions but not staged in cells. (e) 2025 Booker winner (David Szalay's 'Flesh') is OUTSIDE the staged 2000-2024 window and explicitly excluded. (f) Booker eligibility rule change in 2014 (expanded to include US authors) is descriptive context only; the universe is source-defined by the winners table regardless.
- Decision: Stage.

Pre-staging audit design review (2026-05-15): audit agent confirmed the universe (Booker winners 2000-2024), source plan (1 master + 24 per-author), composite PK (Year, Author), claim_type (source_defined), and implicit_join category-fit are all sound. The review surfaced 4 cleanups applied in cycle-0 staging: (1) Use bare birth-country values in CSV cells without parenthetical disambiguations (e.g., 'Spain' not 'Spain (Canadian citizen)' for Yann Martel; 'Canada' not 'Canada (NZ-raised)' for Eleanor Catton; 'United Kingdom' not 'United Kingdom (Northern Ireland)' for Anna Burns; 'United Kingdom' not 'United Kingdom (Scotland)' for Douglas Stuart). (2) Define the birth-country rule precisely: 'Author Birth Country is the modern sovereign country containing the author's birthplace in the per-author article's Born field; constituent countries such as Scotland and Northern Ireland normalize to United Kingdom. Citizenship/nationality/raised-in facts are documented in notes but not included in the cell.' (3) Document the 2025-exclusion explicitly in temporal_note (2025 David Szalay / Flesh is outside the fixed 2000-2024 window). (4) Document the row-count arithmetic: '25 years + 1 extra co-winner row in 2019 = 26 rows'. All 4 cleanups applied in cycle-0 staging.

Post-audit (2026-05-15, cycle 1): cycle-1 audit verdict 'Not ready' — 1 BLOCKING, 1 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE, 0 SUGGESTION. (a) BLOCKING (structural) — draft.json::operation_type was 'implicit_join' but the protocol's canonical operation_type vocabulary requires 'join' for implicit_join-category instances per references/artifact-contract.md. The operation_type values are a closed vocabulary independent of query_category labels even where the names overlap. Resolved by changing draft.json::operation_type from 'implicit_join' to 'join'. The query_category remains 'implicit_join' (the protocol's category-level term); only the operation_type-level term is the canonical 'join' label. (b) HYGIENE (structural) — sort prose claimed the CSV order matches the master Booker article's winners-table order, but the CSV sorts the 2019 co-winner tie alphabetically (Evaristo before Atwood per E < M alphabetical surname order) while the master Booker article's winners table lists the 2019 tie as Atwood before Evaristo (the master's tie-break appears to follow author seniority or announcement order, not alphabetical). Resolved by rewriting the sort-prose to acknowledge the CSV's deterministic (Year, Author) alphabetical-tiebreak sort and explicitly noting that this differs from the master's tie order — the deterministic sort is preferred for an exact-match-evaluable benchmark instance, and the alphabetical tiebreak is the simplest defensible deterministic rule. Net cycle-1 changes: 1 metadata fix (operation_type 'implicit_join' → 'join'); 1 prose-section rewrite (normalization_decisions sort-order paragraph); no CSV / source_count / row count / schema / column / distribution changes (still 26 rows × 4 cols, source_count 25, composite (Year, Author) PK unique, alphabetical-by-Author tie-break sort, 11-distinct-country distribution).

Post-audit (2026-05-15, cycle 2): cycle-2 verification audit verdict 'Ready with residual hygiene' — 0 BLOCKING, 1 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE, 0 SUGGESTION. The cycle-1 fixes were confirmed clean (operation_type=join per protocol; sort-prose departure from master tie-order acknowledged). The single residual hygiene was a wording precision issue in the cycle-1 sort-order prose: the prose said the tiebreak is 'alphabetically by Author surname' but the CSV actually sorts by the full displayed Author field (Bernardine Evaristo before Margaret Atwood — B < M of the full Author cell strings, not surname). Resolved by replacing 'alphabetically by Author surname' with 'alphabetically by the full displayed Author field' and updating the 2019-tie-example explanation from '(E < M)' (surname interpretation) to '(B < M)' (full-cell interpretation). Net cycle-2 changes: 1 prose-section wording precision fix in normalization_decisions sort-order paragraph; no CSV / source_count / row count / schema / distribution / metadata / other-prose changes.

Post-audit (2026-05-15, cycle 3): cycle-3 verification audit verdict 'Ready+Clean' — 0 BLOCKING, 0 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE, 0 SUGGESTION. Cycle-2 sort-prose precision fix confirmed clean: current prose says 'full displayed Author field' and uses '(B < M)' for the 2019-tie explanation. Historical cycle-1 and cycle-2 wording remains only in decision_log paragraphs. CSV 26 rows × 4 cols with unique composite (Year, Author) PK; operation_type='join'; query_category='implicit_join'; source_count=25; Author Birth Country distribution intact. Instance marked accept-ready as of 2026-05-15. Total cycle count: 4 (cycle-0 staging + cycles 1-3 audit/repair). The instance chips `implicit_join` from gap 3 to **gap 2** (6 of 8 staged). Culture/Literature subdomain extends from 1 to 2 instances. NEW `people/authors` fine-class extends the people bucket from 9 to 10 fine-classes. Useful reference: source_defined implicit_join instances with composite-PK + per-entity-article implicit join + curator-bounded time window are clean 3-cycle Ready patterns when pre-staging design review confirms birth-country normalization rule + composite-PK choice + claim_type up-front. The 1 BLOCKING + 2 prose-only HYGIENE arc was small (operation_type vocabulary mismatch + 2 progressive sort-prose precision fixes); pre-staging review missed the operation_type vocabulary mismatch but caught all the universe/source-plan/birth-country issues.
normalization_decisions:
Universe definition: the staged universe is the Booker Prize for Fiction winners 2000-2024 inclusive — a hard 25-year temporal window on the source-defined winners-table membership. Row count = 25 award years + 1 extra row for the 2019 co-winner Bernardine Evaristo + Margaret Atwood shared prize = 26 rows. The Booker Prize Wikipedia article's winners table also lists pre-2000 winners (Atwood 1985, Coetzee 1983/1999, etc.) and a 2025 winner (David Szalay's 'Flesh') — all OUTSIDE the staged window and explicitly excluded. The 25-year window is curator-chosen for LLM-knowability balance (recent + classic Booker winners); membership inside the window is fully source-defined per the master winners table.

Year normalization: each row's Year is the integer year of the award per the master Booker Prize winners table's Year column. Years 2000-2024 inclusive (25 distinct years).

Author normalization: each row's Author is the winning author's name verbatim from the master Booker Prize winners table. Composite PK part 2 (with Year as PK part 1). 24 distinct authors across 26 rows: Hilary Mantel and Margaret Atwood each appear twice (Mantel 2009 + 2012; Atwood 2000 + 2019 co-winner). Author names preserved verbatim from source including pen-name conventions ('DBC Pierre' for Peter Warren Finlay).

Book normalization: each row's Book is the winning book's title verbatim from the master Booker Prize winners table. Includes the comma-separated title 'Girl, Woman, Other' (Evaristo 2019) preserved verbatim. Subtitles preserved per master table convention.

Author Birth Country normalization: each row's Author Birth Country is the modern sovereign country containing the author's birthplace per the per-author Wikipedia article's 'Born' infobox field. The audit-recommended modern-sovereign-country normalization rule applies: 'Author Birth Country is the modern sovereign country containing the author's birthplace in the per-author article's Born field; constituent countries such as Scotland and Northern Ireland normalize to United Kingdom. Citizenship/nationality/raised-in facts are documented in notes but not included in the cell.' Per-row constituent-country normalizations:
  - Anna Burns: born Belfast, Northern Ireland → staged as 'United Kingdom'
  - Douglas Stuart: born Glasgow, Scotland → staged as 'United Kingdom'
  - Alan Hollinghurst: born Stroud, Gloucestershire, England → staged as 'United Kingdom'
  - Hilary Mantel: born Glossop, Derbyshire, England → staged as 'United Kingdom'
  - Howard Jacobson: born Manchester, England → staged as 'United Kingdom'
  - Julian Barnes: born Leicester, England → staged as 'United Kingdom'
  - Bernardine Evaristo: born Eltham, London, England → staged as 'United Kingdom'
  - Samantha Harvey: born Kent, England → staged as 'United Kingdom'

Documented citizenship/raised-in caveats (NOT staged in cells, kept here in notes per audit recommendation):
  - Yann Martel: born Salamanca, Spain (to Canadian-diplomat parents); raised in Canada; Canadian citizen → staged as 'Spain' (birth country) per the Born-field rule.
  - Eleanor Catton: born London, Ontario, Canada (to NZ-academic parents); raised in New Zealand; New Zealand nationality → staged as 'Canada' (birth country) per the Born-field rule.
  - Marlon James: born Kingston, Jamaica; US-resident → staged as 'Jamaica' (birth country).
  - Kiran Desai: born New Delhi, India; US-resident → staged as 'India' (birth country).
  - Anna Burns: identifies as Northern Irish writer; the constituent-country normalization to United Kingdom is documented; some scholarly readings would prefer 'Northern Ireland' as a separate cell value.
  - Douglas Stuart: identifies as Scottish-American writer; the constituent-country normalization to United Kingdom is documented.

Composite PK (Year, Author) handles the 2019 co-winners (Year=2019 + Author=Bernardine Evaristo; Year=2019 + Author=Margaret Atwood — 2 distinct rows) and the within-window 2-time winners (Hilary Mantel 2009+2012; Margaret Atwood 2000+2019).

Sort order: CSV is sorted deterministically by (Year, Author) ascending — Year primary (2000 first → 2024 last) with within-year ties broken alphabetically by the full displayed Author field. The 2019 row order in the staged CSV is Bernardine Evaristo before Margaret Atwood per the alphabetical-by-full-Author-cell tiebreak (B < M). NOTE: this differs from the master Booker Prize Wikipedia article's winners table tie order, which lists the 2019 co-winners as Margaret Atwood before Bernardine Evaristo (the master table's tie-break appears to be by author seniority or by listing order in the announcement, not alphabetical). The staged (Year, Author) deterministic sort departs from the master's tie order intentionally for benchmark-reproducibility — a deterministic sort is preferred for an exact-match-evaluable benchmark instance, and the alphabetical tiebreak is the simplest defensible deterministic rule.
open_questions: 1. Whether the 2000-2024 window is the right universe scope or whether it should be extended (1990-2024 = 35 years) or contracted (2010-2024 = 15 years). Current 25-year window mirrors the LLM-knowability balance of recent+classic winners. 2. Whether constituent-country normalization (Scotland/Northern Ireland → United Kingdom) is the right rule or whether the staged values should preserve Scotland/Northern Ireland as distinct values (would push the closed-vocab beyond modern sovereign countries to include UK constituent nations). 3. Whether the Author Birth Country cell should be Birth-Country-as-Modern-Sovereign-State (current staging) or Birth-Country-at-Time-of-Birth (some authors born before national-boundary changes — none apply within the 2000-2024 window since all authors were born post-WWII). 4. Whether to add a 5th column for Author Birth Year or Author Nationality (audit-noted alternative implicit-join cells); current 4-col schema is consistent with the existing implicit_join precedents. 5. Whether the 2019 co-winners should be staged as 1 row with multi-author cell or 2 rows (current staging) per the composite PK design. 6. Whether the Booker eligibility rule change in 2014 (expansion to include US authors) should be documented in temporal_note (current staging) or in normalization_decisions or both. 7. Whether the Marlon James 'Jamaica' staging is correct or whether it should be 'United States' (US-resident) — current staging uses Jamaica per birth-country rule. 8. Whether the Yann Martel 'Spain' staging is correct or whether 'Canada' (citizenship + raised-in) would be more representative — current staging uses Spain per birth-country rule.
